note: Read 2026-11-01 at the owner's word ("Start the age readers once the ledger lands", the age rules reaching young writers, producers and directors as well as performers; "It should cover across every country"; "Again I want depth covering every basis for every feature leaving NO STONE UNTURNED"): what age changes for screen work in Sri Lanka: the age of majority, the working age, how a minor's contract binds and what of the pay is set aside, a child performer's permit and hours, the unions', the funds' and the company law's ages. Research, retry and web-search subagents (workbench/briefs/BRIEF-ages-roles.md, BRIEF-ages-world.md, BRIEF-ages-search.md), every quote checked by the lead against its saved page. Read again 2026-11-03 in the Government Printer's own copies (documents.gov.lk): the Companies Act No. 7 of 2007, s. 202(2)(a), the director's eighteen; the amending Act No. 8 of 2003, which raised s. 19(1)'s age for a dangerous performance from sixteen to eighteen and changed only s. 18(2)'s penalty; and the amending Act No. 2 of 2021, the child under sixteen. The 1956 Act's s. 18 itself (the entertainment bar) and the Age of Majority Ordinance weren't on the portal, so those figures still rest on LankaLAW.

figures.finding: Sri Lanka's legal age of majority is eighteen (Age of Majority Ordinance No. 7 of 1865 as amended by Act No. 17 of 1989, s. 2), save that a benefit due to a person under twenty-one under another law is kept, and majority may come earlier by operation of law.

sources.said: all persons when they shall attain, or who have already attained, the full age of eighteen years shall be deemed to have attained the legal age of majority

figures.finding: A child may not take part in any entertainment for which any charge (for admission or otherwise) is made to the audience, unless unpaid and for a charitable or educational purpose, by pupils of a public-supervised school, by an amateur dramatic society, or as school training; no one under eighteen may take part in a public performance endangering life or limb. The Act sets no permit, so paid performing before a paying audience is barred to a child (under sixteen since the 2021 amendment); whether filming without an audience is "entertainment" isn't settled in the text.
